the Ab-ACP, a bacterial protein, can be exploited to improve the fatty acid composition of plant seed oil, particularly in the context of the edible oil quality.

the functional expression of Ab-ACp in heterologous hosts has the potential to change the fatty acid composition in a desired manner, which may be exploited in the future to develop new crop varieties with improved oil quality and/or novel bacterial strains with modified lipid composition for biotechnological purposes.

the bacterial A. brasilence-derived Ab-ACP can potentially alter the fatty acid profile of the host system, and the altered profile can be utilized for the improvement of seed oil quality.
